# als — instant static-site / markdown / code publishing CLI

`als` is a single static Rust binary that uploads a folder, a zip, a
single HTML / markdown file, or a directory of source code to the
[a.ls](https://a.ls) service and returns a public URL. It also runs a
local HTTP preview of any of the above. The CLI is the only client an
LLM agent needs — there is no separate REST step.

- Project: <https://a.ls>
- Default API: <https://api.a.ls>  (override with `ALS_API`)
- This file: <https://a.ls/llms.txt>
- Source: <https://github.com/bkhq/als>
- License: MIT

## Install

```
# Linux x64 (static musl)
curl -sSL https://a.ls/releases/latest/als-linux-x64.tar.gz | tar -xz
sudo install -m 0755 ./als /usr/local/bin/als

# macOS / Windows: download the matching archive from
# https://github.com/bkhq/als/releases/latest
```

## One-shot publish (the common case)

```
als auth login            # one time per machine; persists token in
                          # ~/.config/als/config.toml
als ./build               # uploads, prints URL, done
```

The first deploy from a given path remembers the binding in
`~/.config/als/sites/<id>_<name>.toml`. Subsequent `als ./build` runs
from the same checkout push a new version to the same URL — no flags
needed.

## Two identifiers per site

Every site has both:

- **id** — 10-char base32 (`[a-z2-7]{10}`), auto-generated by the
  server, immutable. IS the URL subdomain (`<id>.a.ls`).
- **name** — kebab-case lowercase (`[a-z0-9-]`, no leading or trailing
  `-`), unique per user. With `--name my-proj` you pick it explicitly.
  Without, the CLI mints `<word><NNN>` — a short noun (one of 64
  curated animals / colors / nature words) concatenated with a
  three-digit number, e.g. `fox042` or `mint007`. Easier to read and
  remember than the id; the server is the sole arbiter of name
  uniqueness. Mutable later via `als site <id|name> --name <new>`.

`als <path>`, `als site`, and `als rm` all accept either an `id` or a
`name` wherever they say `<id|name>`. The CLI tries id-shape first and
falls back to a name lookup on miss.

## Common commands

| Command                              | What it does                                                       |
|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `als <path>`                         | Auto-detect (static / markdown / mdbook / code) and publish.       |
| `als <path> --name <name>`           | Pin the project under a stable kebab-case name; URL stays put on every redeploy. |
| `als <path> --pass auto`             | Add a server-generated visitor password.                           |
| `als <path> --expires 7d`            | Set expiration (`5m` / `24h` / `7d` / `1y` / `never` / RFC 3339).  |
| `als <path> --kind code`             | Force the read-only code-viewer rendering on a mixed folder.       |
| `als <path> --new`                   | Force-create a fresh site, ignoring any local pin / server dedup.  |
| `als list`                           | List owned sites with quota footer.                                |
| `als site <id\|name>`                | Detail view + version history.                                     |
| `als site <id\|name> --version <v>`  | Roll back to a past version.                                       |
| `als site <id\|name> --pass auto`    | Rotate or set the visitor password.                                |
| `als site <id\|name> --name <new>`   | Rename (URL unchanged; only the `Name` field shifts).              |
| `als rm <id\|name>`                  | Remove a site (interactive confirm; `-y` to skip).                 |
| `als rm --all-expired -y`            | Batch-remove every expired site.                                   |
| `als unpin <path\|name\|id>`         | Drop the local pin without touching the server.                    |
| `als preview <path>`                 | Local HTTP preview (no network) of what `als <path>` would publish. |
| `als auth status`                    | Active profile, user, quota.                                       |
| `als auth logout`                    | Drop the local token.                                              |
| `als auth revoke`                    | Invalidate the token server-side, then drop locally.               |
| `als config get\|set\|list`          | Inspect / mutate `~/.config/als/config.toml`.                      |

Global flags accepted by every subcommand:

- `--profile <name>` — switch to a named profile from the config file.
- `--quiet` — emit only the essential line (typically the URL).
- `--json` — emit a machine-readable JSON envelope.

## Auto-detection rules for `als <path>`

| Input                                              | Mode |
|----------------------------------------------------|------|
| Folder with `index.html`                           | site — recursive zip |
| Folder with `book.toml`                            | site — mdbook build, then zip |
| Folder with `*.md` (no `book.toml`)                | site — auto-bootstrap mdbook |
| Single `.html`                                     | site — wrapped as `<stem>/index.html` |
| Single `.md`                                       | site — one-chapter mdbook |
| `.zip` archive                                     | site — uploaded as-is |
| Folder of recognised source code (no html / md)    | code — viewer shell + manifest + raw/ |
| Single recognised code file                        | code — viewer shell with one file |

`--kind site` / `--kind code` forces the routing decision.

## Per-project config: `als.toml`

Optional file at the input root. Always dropped from the bundle.

```toml
# Every field optional; unknown fields error out.

title        = "DemoForAcme"          # code mode: viewer <title>; default: folder name
default_file = "src/main.rs"          # code mode: viewer opens this first;
                                      #           must exist after `exclude` filter
exclude      = ["scratch/**", "*.log", "!keep.log"]
                                      # extra ignore patterns; applies to every mode;
                                      # gitignore syntax with `!` negation
```

| Field          | Modes      | Effect                                                            |
|----------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `title`        | code only  | Viewer page title.                                                |
| `default_file` | code only  | File the viewer opens on load; must be in the bundled file set.   |
| `exclude`      | every mode | Extra gitignore patterns layered on top of the default ignores.   |

## Default ignored paths (every deploy)

```
.git/  .svn/  .hg/  node_modules/  target/  dist/  __pycache__/
.DS_Store  Thumbs.db  .env  *.pem  *.key
```

`als.toml.exclude` layers on top; gitignore syntax with negation
overriding the defaults.

## Code-mode limits

| Limit                              | Value          |
|------------------------------------|----------------|
| Files (after ignore filter)        | ≤ 50           |
| Per-file size                      | ≤ 256 KB       |
| Total size                         | ≤ 2 MB         |
| Directory depth                    | ≤ 8            |

Binary files (detected by NUL / non-printables in the first 1024 bytes)
are skipped automatically.

## Output modes

| Selector  | Behaviour                                                       |
|-----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| (default) | Human, coloured + decorated text; ANSI auto-strips on pipes.    |
| `--quiet` | Decoration-free; emits the essential line only.                 |
| `--json`  | Machine-readable JSON envelope.                                 |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning                                                              |
|------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `0`  | Success                                                              |
| `1`  | General / sentinel errors (`archive_too_large`, `code_*`, …)         |
| `2`  | Usage error (clap parse failure)                                     |
| `3`  | Authentication (401)                                                 |
| `4`  | Network (DNS / connect / read timeout)                               |
| `5`  | Server error (5xx)                                                   |
| `6`  | Quota exceeded (402)                                                 |
| `7`  | Rate limited (429)                                                   |

JSON mode preserves the same exit codes; the failure body is emitted
as `{"error":{"code":"<sentinel>","message":"..."}}` on stderr.

## Environment overrides

| Variable      | Effect                                              |
|---------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| `ALS_API`    | Override the active profile's API URL.              |
| `ALS_TOKEN`  | Override the active profile's bearer token.         |
| `ALS_PROFILE`| Select a named profile.                             |
| `ALS_TRANSPORT` | Force the transport for this invocation: `h3` / `h2` / `auto`. Unset = consult `[transport."<host:port>"]` in `~/.config/als/config.toml` (user-managed; the CLI never writes it). `"h3"` / `"h2"` are hard force, `"auto"` (and missing) probes once per session and falls back in-memory. |

## End-to-end example (agent-friendly)

```
# 1. Log in once (device flow; copy the printed URL into any browser).
als auth login

# 2. Publish a static site with a stable name. Output shows two
#    identifiers: `Id` (URL subdomain) and `Name` (your label).
#    Without --name the CLI mints e.g. `fox042` (a memorable word
#    plus 3 digits).
als ./dist --name demosite
# ✓ Deployed: https://k7x2qm4j6p.a.ls
#   Id:      k7x2qm4j6p
#   Name:    demosite

# 3. Re-publish to the same URL with a fresh version (no flags needed,
#    the local pin remembers the binding).
als ./dist

# 4. Add a password without redeploying. Either id or name works.
als site demosite --pass auto

# 5. Inspect / list.
als list
als site demosite

# 6. Tear down.
als rm demosite -y
```

## When in doubt

- `als help` and `als <command> --help` both render full usage.
- `als --json` is stable; build scripts and agents should prefer it.
- `als preview <path>` is offline and never touches the network.
